newsitem.title: BURMA: Military closes roads around Rangoon universities.
newsitem.headline: Military closes roads around Rangoon universities.

text.p: Burma's military authorities on Sunday kept some roads closed around two universities in northern Rangoon near where soldiers and police broke up a student protest the day before, witnesses said.

The atmosphere around the University of Yangon (Rangoon) and the Yangon Institute of Technology (YIT) was tense as armed troops and police manned some sections of the main and side roads linking the two institutions, they told Reuters.
"The atmosphere is visibly tense. I saw about 350 helmeted soldiers near one intersection last night," a witness said.
Elsewhere the capital Rangoon was calm.

The road closures followed a night filled with rumours in Rangoon that the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) might impose a night curfew after breaking up the student protest at a road junction near Yangon University early on Saturday.

There were also rumours the SLORC might close the two institutions, whose students last week staged the two biggest protests seen in Rangoon since pro-democracy uprisings in 1988 were crushed by the military, leaving thousands dead or in jail.
The SLORC has made no comment in response to the rumours.

The authorities also continued to bar access to the residence of opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi in an apparent attempt to prevent her from holding public gatherings and as a preventive measure to keep her away from the student protests.

Early on Saturday, troops and police used water cannons to break up the student protest near Yangon University. More than 260 protesters who refused to disperse despite pleas by government officials were detained but later released.
The students had demanded among other things they be allowed to set up student unions in campuses and the release of some 80 colleagues they claimed were detained in a separate incident.

Many witnesses said they heard anti-government chanting by students near a campus compound close to Yangon University on Saturday night. But they could not give any details because the area was sealed off from the public.
Diplomats said the closure of the roads was a government attempt to cut off links between the two institutions.

In a demonstration last Monday and Tuesday, up to 2,000 students from the two institutions held a street protest that culminated in the police detention of more than 600 protesters in central Rangoon early on Tuesday. They were later freed.

The protesters had demanded then that the government publish action taken against policemen who had treated some of their colleagues unfairly during a brawl between YIT students and restaurant owners in October.
The students claimed their protests were non-political but they also demanded more rights and freedom.
Aides to Suu Kyi told Reuters the Nobel peace laureate had not left her house since Friday, although government officials said she had freedom of movement since Thursday.
She was confined to her house temporarily last Tuesday and Wednesday after the students first protested.
Suu Kyi and the student leaders have denied any links to each other, but her supporters said there was a moral tie between the two parties.
